title: Copilot Studio: discover and add skills from the skills catalog
summary: Hold: the advice to treat the capability as arriving without an administrator switch goes beyond the evidence. Microsoft documents environment-level skills controls, but their coverage of the preview browsing and sharing flow is not established; the briefing must preserve that uncertainty rather than assume no switch.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans a Copilot Studio catalog for makers to discover, reuse and selectively share approved organisational skills.
claims.quote: makers can discover, reuse and selectively share approved organizational skills instead of recreating the same instructions and workflows for every agent

claims.claim: The planned shared catalog is powered by Microsoft 365 App Store.
claims.quote: The shared catalog powered by Microsoft 365 App Store

claims.claim: The roadmap says shared skills can extend across Copilot Studio, Microsoft 365 Copilot and Cowork.
claims.quote: enables shared skills to extend across experiences such as Copilot Studio M365 copilot, and Cowork

claims.claim: The roadmap describes maintaining centralised governance.
claims.quote: helping organizations standardize proven ways of working while maintaining centralized governance

claims.quote: Select the Build tab. ... Select the + icon next to Skills, and then select Browse skills (preview). ... Select the skill you want to add. ... On the skill details page, select Add.

claims.claim: The available shared skills are those shared by administrators or skill owners.
claims.quote: The skills available to you are the ones shared by admins or skill owners.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope; controls[3].note
claims.claim: The browse and share flows are preview documentation subject to change.
claims.quote: Browse and add shared skills (preview) ... Share a skill (preview) ... This article contains Microsoft Copilot Studio preview documentation and is subject to change.

claims.claim: Learn does not explicitly equate Browse skills with the catalog described in the roadmap.
claims.quote: Searched: "skills catalog" "Copilot Studio" and Copilot Studio "skills catalog" "Browse skills" admin disable sharing API skill table licensing. Read skills-manage, skills-overview and whats-new; none explicitly identifies roadmap item 571880 or equates its named catalog with Browse skills.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A skill has a name, description and instructions that guide the agent's handling of a task.
claims.quote: A skill is a capability defined by a name, a description, and instructions that tell the agent how to handle specific types of tasks or scenarios.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Adding a shared skill gives the agent a snapshot with a reference to the original.
claims.quote: When you add a shared skill, the agent gets a snapshot of the skill while maintaining a reference to the original shared skill.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Opening an agent that uses an older shared skill version produces an update notification.
claims.quote: You receive a skill update notification when you open an agent that uses an older version of a shared skill.

claims.claim: Makers can choose to update to the new shared skill version.
claims.quote: You can choose to update to the new version by selecting the update button for the skill.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: A maker chooses the audience when sharing a skill they created.
claims.quote: When you share a skill you created, you and other people in your organization can use it in their Copilot Studio agents. You can keep the skill private or share it with specific people or groups in your organization.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; controls[3].note
claims.claim: The detailed preview sharing instructions offer Only you or Specific users or groups in your organization.
claims.quote: Only you: Keeps the skill private to your account. ... Specific users or groups in your organization: Lets you add people or groups by name or email address.
claims.fix: Add: "The What's new page also describes sharing with your whole organisation, whereas the detailed sharing instructions list Only you and specific users or groups." Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/whats-new#notable-changes, which says "share your own skills with specific people or your whole organization".

claims.claim: Recipients of a shared skill can add it to their agents.
claims.quote: The people and groups you share with can then add the skill to their agents.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: An owner must share an edited shared skill again to make the latest version available.
claims.quote: When you edit and change a skill that you already shared, share the skill again to make the latest version available to those you previously shared it with.

claims.claim: A skill package can include supporting scripts, templates and reference documents.
claims.quote: The package can optionally include supporting files, such as scripts, templates, and reference documents.

claims.claim: The Learn skills documentation does not specify the data-access boundaries of a catalog skill.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Studio" "shared skill" "data access". Read skills-manage, skills-overview and skills-add-existing; results discuss apps and connected agents, but do not define catalog-skill data-access boundaries.

claims.claim: The runtime decides when to activate a skill from the user's message and skill description, without requiring the user to name it.
claims.quote: The orchestration runtime decides when to activate a skill based on the user's message and the skill's description.

claims.claim: A skill can instruct an agent to use a specific tool.
claims.quote: For example, a skill might instruct your agent to use a specific tool in a particular way.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft does not document a catalog approval step beyond the maker selecting Add to add a shared skill.
claims.quote: Searched: "Browse skills" "approval" "Copilot Studio"; "Copilot Studio" "skills" "catalog" administrator role approval data access. Read skills-manage and manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers; the shared-skill flow ends at Add and no catalog-specific approval procedure is stated.

claims.claim: The documented maker capability is user-opt-in.
claims.quote: Select the + icon next to Skills, and then select Browse skills (preview). ... On the skill details page, select Add. Searched: "Copilot Studio" "Browse skills" "disable"; no enablement prerequisite for this specific flow was stated.

claims.claim: Administrators should treat the capability as arriving without an administrator switch until Microsoft documents one.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Studio" "Browse skills" "disable"; "Copilot Studio" "skill sharing" "tenant". Read skills-manage and power-platform/admin/skills-copilot-studio-rule: the latter documents environment skills controls but does not resolve their coverage of Browse skills.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence with: "The wiki's view: no source says existing agent behaviour changes; confirm which controls apply to Browse skills before relying on package controls." Do not turn the lack of a catalog-specific procedure into an assumption that no administrator switch governs the capability.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not specified a catalog-specific administrator action or what happens on the catalog's arrival.
claims.quote: Searched: "skills catalog" "Copilot Studio"; Copilot Studio "skills catalog" "Browse skills" admin disable sharing API skill table licensing. Read the roadmap, skills-manage, whats-new and skills-copilot-studio-rule; no catalog rollout notice or required catalog-specific administrator action is stated.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn documents no tenant-level switch specifically for sharing a maker-created skill.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Studio" "skill sharing" "tenant" and "Copilot Studio" "skill" "sharing" "API" Power Platform pac admin. Read skills-manage and skills-copilot-studio-rule; the latter governs skill types, not a tenant-wide maker-skill sharing switch.

claims.claim: No API for the maker's Share a skill control is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio shared skills sharing skill Dataverse table entity reference API tenant controls; "Copilot Studio" "skill" "sharing" "API" Power Platform pac admin. Read skills-manage and package API overview; Dynamics skill tables returned by search do not identify this sharing control.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: User availability for a plugin or skill package is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Plugins > plugin or skill > Users.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Tools > Plugins. ... Select the plugin that you want to manage. ... Open Users ... Managing a skill uses the same actions and steps as managing a plugin.

claims.claim: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id} updates package user availability.
claims.quote: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id} ... allowedUsersAndGroups ... Users/groups for whom the package is available.

claims.claim: The package update and block APIs are preview.
claims.quote: Update package (preview) ... PATCH /copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id} ... Block (preview) ... POST /copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.where: controls[0].note; controls[2].note; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 licence.
claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.

claims.claim: The update request body uses availableTo and allowedUsersAndGroups to set user availability.
claims.quote: allowedUsersAndGroups ... Users/groups for whom the package is available. ... availableTo ... Enum value specifying which users or groups within the tenant can access this package. Required if updating allowedUsersAndGroups.

claims.where: controls[0].note; controls[1].note; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft does not explicitly confirm that these package controls govern the named Copilot Studio skills catalog.
claims.quote: Searched: "skills catalog" "Copilot Studio"; "Copilot Studio" "skills" "catalog" administrator role approval data access. Read manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers, administrator-guide, package overview and skills-manage; package scope is documented, but the catalog's identity is not explicitly established.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Blocking a skill package follows Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Plugins > skill > Block > Block.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Tools > Plugins. ... From the list, select the plugin or skill that you want to block. ... Select Block, and then select Block again to confirm.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block prevents package usage.
claims.quote: Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage. ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Package controls cover standalone skill packages; a bundled skill has no separate blocking control.
claims.quote: For a bundled skill, apply the plugin's controls. You can't block an individual skill inside a package today.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Package inventory is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Registry.
claims.quote: Use Agents > Tools > Registry to review plugin and separately packaged skill records in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/copilot/admin/catalog/packages?$filter=elementTypes/any(e:e eq 'AgentSkills') lists packages containing skills.

claims.claim: It is not explicitly confirmed that the inventory lists the named Copilot Studio catalog's skills.
claims.quote: Searched: "skills catalog" "Copilot Studio" and Copilot Studio skills catalog browse add share skill Copilot Credits rate license prerequisites. Read package overview, copilotpackages-list, administrator-guide and skills-manage; no explicit mapping of this catalog to package inventory was stated.

claims.where: controls[3].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The maker sharing route is Agents > agent > Build > skill > more options > Share > Share.
claims.quote: Select the Build tab. ... the Skills section shows the skills ... Select the skill you want to share ... Select the three dots (...) and then select Share. ... On the details page, select Share in the upper-right corner.
claims.fix: Include the omitted Skills section heading in both representations: "Agents > agent > Build > Skills > skill > … > Share > Share". The already-cited https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent supplies the starting step: "Open the agent from the Agents page".

claims.claim: Copilot Studio and Power Platform can have separate controls for components and connections.
claims.quote: Copilot Studio and Power Platform can have separate controls for their components and connections.

claims.claim: Some skills used in Word, Excel and PowerPoint are stored in OneDrive rather than the plugin registry.
claims.quote: Don't assume every skill is stored in the plugin registry. Skills used in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint are stored in OneDrive today.

claims.claim: Agents > Settings > Agent and plugin access sets publisher categories for plugin access in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Settings > Agent and plugin access. ... choose which publisher categories users can access: Microsoft, your organization, or certified external publishers.

claims.claim: Consumption is the documented billing model for the supporting Microsoft Copilot harness experience.
claims.quote: Agents, workflows, and apps powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness ... use a usage-based billing structure. ... Usage is billed based on consumption and measured in Copilot Credits.

claims.quote: The harness used to build this agent uses usage-based billing. Using, building, testing, and evaluating agents might consume Copilot Credits.

claims.quote: Unlike the standard harness, which starts billing after publish, the Microsoft Copilot harness charges credits from the moment you start building.

claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio skills catalog browse add share skill Copilot Credits rate license prerequisites. Read skills-manage, skills-add-existing and billing-credit-overview; they state harness consumption but no separate browsing, adding or sharing skill rate.

claims.claim: Agents using shared skills remain subject to the documented harness billing.

claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Studio" "skills" "catalog" administrator role approval data access. Read skills-manage, skills-overview and manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers; search gives general authoring roles but no role requirement for the named catalog.

claims.claim: The cited plugin-management page names AI Administrator and Global Administrator for approving MCP server requests, not as skill-specific roles.
claims.quote: To complete the review and approval process ... access to the Tools page ... grant tenant-wide consent. Two roles meet both requirements: AI Administrator. Global Administrator.

claims.claim: The Customer Conversation harness has Generative and Topic skill types.
claims.quote: Agents powered by the Customer Conversation harness support two types of skills: Generative skills ... and Topic skills, which are deterministic, authored flows of steps and conditions.

claims.claim: The shared-skill section does not explicitly enumerate the harnesses covered by Browse skills.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio "skills catalog" "Browse skills" admin disable sharing API skill table licensing. Read skills-manage and skills-overview; the shared-skill instructions do not enumerate supported harnesses, while the overview enumerates harness-specific creation methods separately.

claims.claim: Variable cost reflects the published Copilot Credits meter for the supporting harness experience, rather than a separate catalog charge.
claims.quote: Usage is billed based on consumption and measured in Copilot Credits. Creating and using agents, workflows, and apps consumes credits based on usage and rate of consumption.
